title: Measuring Progress in Reasoning Toward Mathematical Discovery with Automatic Verification
abstract: arXiv:2603.15617v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Can AI make progress on important, unsolved mathematical problems? Large language models are now capable of sophisticated mathematical and scientific reasoning, but whether they can perform novel research is still widely debated and underexplored. We introduce HorizonMath, a benchmark of 113 predominantly unsolved problems spanning eight domains in mathematics and the mathematical sciences, paired with an open-source evaluation framework for automated verification. Our benchmark targets the generator-verifier gap: problems where discovery is hard and requires meaningful mathematical insight, but verification is computationally straightforward. This contrasts with most existing research-level benchmarks, which instead rely on formal proof verification or manual review, both of which are expensive to scale. translated_title: 基于自动验证的数学发现推理进展测量
translated_abstract: AI能否在重要的未解决数学问题上取得进展？大型语言模型如今已具备复杂的数学和科学推理能力，但它们能否开展真正新颖的研究仍被广泛争论且探索不足。我们提出了HorizonMath，这是一个包含113个以未解决问题为主的基准，涵盖数学与数学科学领域的八个方向，并配有一个用于自动验证的开源评估框架。我们的基准瞄准的是“生成-验证差距”：即那些发现困难、需要实质性数学洞察，但验证在计算上简单直接的问题。这与大多数现有研究级基准形成鲜明对比，后者依赖形式化证明验证或人工审查，而这两者都难以规模化扩展。由于这些问题的解是未知的，HorizonMath能够抵抗数据污染，且大多数最先进的模型得分低于……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了HorizonMath基准，包含113个涵盖八个数学领域的未解决问题，利用“发现难、验证易”的自动验证框架评估AI的数学发现能力，兼具抗数据污染和易于规模化评估的优势。
en_tdlr: Introduces HorizonMath, a benchmark of 113 unsolved problems across eight mathematical domains paired with an open-source automated verification framework, targeting the generator-verifier gap to enable contamination-resistant and scalable evaluation of AI's mathematical discovery capabilities.
